- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75.0), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent high or adjust downward if sentiment turns neutral/negative.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model frequently underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast mean to compensate for downward bias.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue falling; adjust upward toward prior 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth forecast curve using 7-day moving average to reduce volatility.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model underestimates further drop; add 1–2% to forecast to reflect stronger downward momentum.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is rising, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
- Forecast should not exceed 10% above or below 14-day moving average unless sentiment strongly supports it.
